title: WHO issues global guideline on the use of GLP-1 medicines in treating obesity
key_claim: WHO issues first global guideline on GLP-1 therapies for obesity; calls for pooled procurement, tiered pricing, voluntary licensing; projects <10% of those who could benefit will be reached by 2030 even with rapid expansion.
notes: Structural anchor - canonical primary source for the global access framing of the signal.

title: Financial report for the period 1 January 2026 to 31 March 2026
key_claim: Novo Nordisk raised 2026 guidance after Q1 driven by Wegovy oral pill ($353M Q1 sales), expanded Wegovy footprint to 55+ countries, launched second brands Poviztra and Extensior in India and Brazil to fend off generic competition.
notes: Primary corporate disclosure - innovator response to patent geography fracture.

title: Making treatment for obesity more equitable
key_claim: Patents for semaglutide expire in 2026 in Brazil, Canada, China, India and Türkiye - countries accounting for ~40% of the world's population; 2026 may prove a pivotal year for obesity equity.
notes: Peer-reviewed framing of the global equity inflection.

title: Your Questions Answered: Off-patent Semaglutide in 2026
key_claim: Global obesity medicines market reached $66B in 2025, forecast to rise to $92B in 2026 and $105-200B by 2027+; markets losing exclusivity (India, China, Brazil, Türkiye, Canada) account for 38% of adults living with obesity globally; oral GLP-1s and next-gen medicines will capture premium segments while low-cost semaglutide captures price-sensitive markets.
notes: Authoritative institutional forecast of the bifurcation.

title: How Low Could Semaglutide Prices Fall? An Analysis of Production Cost and Implications for Global Access Ahead of Patent Expiry
key_claim: Generic injectable semaglutide could be produced for $28 per person-year; by end of 2026, generic injectable semaglutide could be available in 160 countries covering 84% of the global obesity burden; over 80 companies marketing or registering generic GLP-1 formulations across 11 countries.
notes: Academic production-cost analysis - quantification anchor for the access pivot.

title: Novo further cuts semaglutide prices as generics enter India
key_claim: Novo Nordisk cut Wegovy India prices by 48% and Ozempic by 36%; branded semaglutide previously >Rs 10,000/month, generics now offered below Rs 2,000/month (90% reduction); 50+ generic brands launched after India patent expired March 2026.
notes: Quality journalism with primary-source quotes from Novo India MD and specific NPPA-filing-based pricing data.

title: India is launching cheap weight-loss drugs - but Novo Nordisk is betting its brands will stay on top
key_claim: Smaller Indian manufacturers (Natco, Alkem) discounting semaglutide nearly 80% below Novo; Sun Pharma and Dr Reddy's launching at ~50% below innovator prices; 32,000 units of Wegovy/Ozempic sold in India in April 2026 (first full month post-generic entry).
notes: International business journalism on innovator-generic competitive dynamics.

title: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Launches its Generic Semaglutide Injection in Canada
key_claim: Dr Reddy's received Health Canada Notice of Compliance 28 April 2026; first company to receive Health Canada approval for generic semaglutide; Canada is first G7 country to grant market authorization for generic semaglutide injection; launched Obeda brand in India.
notes: Corporate press release - first G7 generic approval is a structural marker.
